findings.title: Explicit `render :show` makes `show` render before `canonical_url` is set
findings.body: `perform_show_response` now calls `render :show` inside the `format.html` block. In `show`, `perform_show_response` is called first and `canonical_url UrlHelper.absolute_without_cdn(...)` is called right after it. Previously the template rendered implicitly after the action returned, so the canonical URL was set before the layout ran. Now the view and layout are rendered immediately inside `perform_show_response`, so the later `canonical_url` call has no effect on the HTML. Topic pages will lose the correct `<link rel="canonical">` and fall back to the request URL, for example `/t/slug/id/5`. That is an SEO regression on every topic page. Fix by calling `canonical_url` before `perform_show_response`, or by rendering only in `unsubscribe`.

findings.title: `TopicUser.find_by` can return nil, causing a 500 in `unsubscribe`
findings.body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` returns nil when the logged-in user has no `topic_users` row for that topic, which is the case for any other user who opens the URL. The next line, `tu.notification_level`, then raises NoMethodError and the user gets a 500 error page. The action should create the row, for example via `TopicUser.change`, or handle the nil case.

findings.title: Notification level changed with `save!` instead of `TopicUser.change`
findings.body: The action sets `tu.notification_level` directly and calls `tu.save!`. This bypasses `TopicUser.change`, which also sets `notifications_changed_at` and `notifications_reason_id` (user_changed) and publishes the `notification_level_change` MessageBus message. With `notifications_reason_id` left unchanged (often NULL), `TopicUser.update_last_read` will later auto-promote the topic back to `tracking` once the user has read enough. That silently undoes the mute or unsubscribe. Open clients also never receive the level change. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`.

findings.title: State-changing, non-idempotent toggle behind a GET route
findings.body: `unsubscribe` is routed as a GET and mutates the user's notification level on every request. Each reload or repeat visit steps it down further: watching/tracking becomes regular, regular becomes muted, muted stays muted. A single click followed by a refresh, or the back button, therefore mutes the topic instead of just unsubscribing. Because it is a GET with no CSRF protection, any third-party page that embeds `` can mute topics for a logged-in visitor. The `.json` format variant mutates as well. The action should compute a deterministic target state, or require an explicit POST/PUT from the confirmation page.

findings.title: `unsubscribe_link` string now requires `%{unsubscribe_url}`, which breaks callers that omit it
findings.body: The English `unsubscribe_link` string now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Both `html_part` (line 67) and `body` (line 90) call `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`. Any caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` (other mailers, plugins, existing specs) now raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` when the email is built. The spec had to be edited to pass `unsubscribe_url` for exactly this reason. The builder should supply a fallback or only include the per-topic sentence when `unsubscribe_url` is present.

findings.title: No tests for the new unsubscribe action, URL helper, or email content
findings.body: The only spec change adds an `unsubscribe_url` option to an existing message-builder example. There is no controller spec for `TopicsController#unsubscribe`: login required, slug redirect, level transitions, missing `TopicUser` row, JSON vs HTML. There is no spec for `Topic#unsubscribe_url`. There is no spec that the notification email actually contains the per-topic unsubscribe link in both the HTML and text parts. The nil-`TopicUser` crash and the idempotency problem above would have been caught by such tests.
